requirement.title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

acceptance_criteria.text: Neither the generator (CS8785) nor the analyzer (AD0001) crashes when a [MessagePackObject] type has a member whose type is a closed generic value type (struct or record struct) declared in a referenced assembly.
In that case, the consuming assembly gets a generated resolver that provides a formatter for the type.
At runtime, such a type round-trips (serialize then deserialize) with the generated resolver.
Cases that already worked (non-generic struct, generic class, generic struct declared in the same assembly) keep working.
acceptance_criteria.status: supported without a passing linked test

claims.text: Closed generic types from a referenced assembly, including generic value types and record structs, can be used as members of [MessagePackObject] types.
Diagnostics about members of such a type are reported by the defining assembly, not by the consuming project (the analyzer only reports on members declared in the project being compiled).
Tests cover closed generic structs and record structs from a metadata reference.

findings.title: Diagnostics are filtered by a wrapper, but the crash fix itself is not shown; the metadata-declared struct path (e.g. DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] elsewhere) may still throw

findings.title: Diagnostic.Create with a null location passes the filter check only via the wrapper. Diagnostics for metadata members are silently dropped, including ones the consuming project may legitimately want (e.g. the type is unusable). This hides real problems for referenced types.

findings.title: No test performs a runtime serialize/deserialize round trip, so AC-3 is not covered
findings.verification_note: Executed proofs show the affected criteria hold; kept for the owner to judge.

findings.title: Resolver check only asserts the resolver file hint name exists, not that it contains a formatter for the generic struct (AC-2). The main test also skips generated-source comparison.
findings.verification_note: Quote found; no proof covers it.

findings.title: Tests only pass LanguageVersion.CSharp7_3 for the plain struct case, and the unkeyed-member test expects zero diagnostics, which encodes the silent-drop behaviour as correct; it does not verify the analyzer is never invoked on metadata types for the other crash site (AD0001).
findings.verification_note: Quote found; no proof covers it.

findings.title: README states closed generic types from referenced assemblies work, but the defining type is only checked for diagnostics, not that the defining assembly's [MessagePackObject] attribute is honored at runtime
findings.quote: Closed generic types defined in a referenced assembly (for example, `Item<int>` where `Item<T>` is defined in another project or NuGet package) can be used as members of your `[MessagePackObject]` types, including generic value types and record structs.

refusals.why: This is a user-visible behaviour decision about which diagnostics users see. It is not something I can settle by reading the code.

refusals.question: Does the claim that diagnostics are reported by the defining assembly hold for all consumers, for example when the referenced assembly was built without the analyzer?
refusals.why: I can't check by reading whether the defining assembly ran the analyzer. The claim depends on build setups outside this diff.
